about: Wire-colour profiles for cabinets whose drawing set has no wire-colour legend. A profile is used only when someone chooses it for the project; the cabinet's own wire list or drawing legend always comes first (wire_rules.py). Colour codes are IEC 60757 (BK black, BN brown, RD red, OG orange, YE yellow, GN green, BU blue, VT violet, GY grey, WH white, PK pink, TQ turquoise; 'GN/YE' green-and-yellow, 'WH/BU' white with a blue stripe). Classes: AC and DC are the cabinet's mains and DC distribution, ALARM the signalling contacts, PE protective earth. The values summarise secondary sources; each profile names the edition to check against the standard itself.

iec-60204-1.name: IEC 60204-1 (machinery, international / EU)

meaning.OG: circuits fed from an external source that stay live with the main switch off

iec-60204-1.verify: IEC 60204-1 recommends these colours where colour coding is used; only green-and-yellow for the protective conductor is mandatory. Check the edition named in the project specification.

nfpa-79.name: NFPA 79 (industrial machinery, USA)
nfpa-79.edition: NFPA 79 (2024 edition), chapter 13 conductor identification; UL 508A has parallel rules

meaning.YE: control circuits that stay live with the disconnect off (also OG)
meaning.GN: equipment grounding conductor (with or without yellow stripes)

nfpa-79.verify: Section numbers differ between NFPA 79 editions; check the edition and any UL 508A listing the project requires.

iec-60445.name: IEC 60445 harmonised (BS 7671, current Indian and Australian practice)
iec-60445.region: UK, EU installations, India (current), Australia / NZ (2018 edition)
iec-60445.edition: IEC 60445:2021; BS 7671:2018 Table 51; IS 732 current edition; AS/NZS 3000:2018

meaning.BN: line L1 (single phase: line); DC positive L+
meaning.BU: neutral (light blue); DC mid-wire or earthed conductor M

iec-60445.verify: IEC 60445 sets no colours for control or alarm circuits, so alarm wiring is only checked for the green-and-yellow rule. The Indian and Australian editions are reported to follow these colours; confirm against the standard in force for the project.

is-732-legacy.name: India, legacy practice (IS 732:1989 era)
is-732-legacy.edition: IS 732:1989 practice; current Indian practice follows the IEC 60445 colours
is-732-legacy.verify: Legacy scheme: black is the NEUTRAL here but a phase under IEC 60445, so never mix the two profiles. Use it only for older cabinets or where the client specifies it.

as-nzs-3000-legacy.name: Australia / NZ, legacy practice (AS/NZS 3000:2000)
as-nzs-3000-legacy.edition: AS/NZS 3000:2000 Table 3.5; the 2018 edition is reported to use the IEC 60445 colours
as-nzs-3000-legacy.verify: Recommended colours of the 2000 edition; confirm against the purchased AS/NZS 3000 edition the project is built to.
